name: Bubble Break ASMR Tabletop
request: Create a small, playable Bubble Break ASMR game for one player on desktop and touch. The player presses individual bubbles on a reusable bubble-wrap sheet. A press visibly depresses and pops that bubble with synchronized satisfying pop audio, then adds exactly one to the popped counter after the pop completes. Holding, spamming, or pressing a popped bubble must not count twice. Let the player finish a sheet of at least twelve bubbles, see completion feedback, and deliberately reset to a fresh sheet. Use a close, readable tabletop presentation and minimal counter/reset UI. Search Marketplace first for a complete reusable interaction, including any existing geometry, animation, sounds and behavior; inspect what it already provides and integrate only missing features. Search separately for missing media if needed. Audio must come from Marketplace and actually play. Record unavailable importer capabilities rather than pretending a suitable scripted component does not exist. Choose reasonable details yourself; no saving, multiplayer, purchases or large map. Success needs observed press/pop/recovery timing, per-bubble state, exact counting, sheet completion/reset and usable desktop/touch input. Do not claim success from code inspection alone.

assetNeeds.role: Complete reusable bubble-wrap interaction system to supply as much of the individual bubble geometry, press detection, pop animation, state behavior, and embedded media as can be safely preserved.
assetNeeds.constraints: Inspect the full hierarchy, scripts, dependencies, animations, interaction interfaces, and sound references before assigning replacement work. Candidate should expose at least 12 individually pressable bubbles, support click or tap interaction, and fit a compact tabletop area. Audit all source; reject arbitrary HTTP execution and numeric require IDs. Unsupported script, rig, animation, or serialization import is a capability gap requiring explicit escalation, not permission to recreate the component procedurally. Native tests must establish which claimed behavior and media actually function.

intent.experienceRole: This component is the tactile centerpiece of the requested ASMR loop and should preserve any useful existing bubble geometry, depression/pop motion, interaction behavior, and media rather than reducing the Marketplace search to a decorative prop.
intent.interaction: The player selects one intact bubble by mouse or touch, observes a brief depression followed by its pop and settled popped state, hears synchronized audio, and receives one counter increment only after that pop finishes. Repeated, held, or overlapping input on the same bubble must be ignored.
reusableFeatures: Individually addressable bubble geometry and intact/popping/popped states
Existing desktop and touch interaction handling
Existing depression, pop, settle, or recovery animation timing
Embedded Marketplace sound references and playback placement
Completion or reset behavior that can be safely retained
Documented events, attributes, modules, or callbacks usable for counter integration

assetNeeds.role: Marketplace-sourced close, satisfying bubble-wrap pop sound used for every successful bubble pop when the retained component does not already contain a suitable verified sound.
assetNeeds.constraints: First inspect and prefer relevant captured sounds from the retained interaction component. Otherwise search Marketplace separately. The selected audio must load, play, and be listened to in native gameplay; confirm audible synchronization with the visible pop completion at the tabletop camera. Do not use generated, built-in, procedural, placeholder, or invented audio IDs. If no suitable audio can be imported and verified, report the audio requirement as blocked.

intent.experienceRole: The synchronized pop is essential ASMR feedback and confirms that a valid bubble transitioned from pressed to popped.
intent.interaction: A successful intact-bubble press triggers one audible pop aligned with the visible pop phase; rejected repeat, hold, spam, or popped-bubble inputs produce no additional pop sound or reward.
reusableFeatures: Relevant embedded sound already referenced by the retained component
Clean transient bubble-pop character without unrelated speech or music
Reliable loading and playback through a preserved Marketplace reference
Playback behavior suitable for rapid but distinct presses
Existing spatial emitter or sound attachment near the sheet

spec.assetStrategy: Discovery begins with a complete reusable bubble-wrap interaction Model, not separate decorative bubble meshes. The selected candidate must be inspected for individually addressable geometry, state handling, click/tap support, animation, embedded audio, completion/reset behavior, scripts, dependencies, and integration interfaces. Useful verified behavior and media will be retained; only gaps established by that inspection may receive integration work. The model acquisition and audit are blocking because importer or capability limitations do not authorize silently rebuilding an apparently suitable scripted component. The separate Audio need represents the mandatory pop-audio obligation: retained component audio is preferred, but it still requires provenance, loading, playback, synchronization, and listening checks; Marketplace search supplies missing audio when necessary. No asset IDs, interfaces, or final glue-script ownership are assumed before discovery. If source auditing, animation preservation, sound capture, or importer support cannot preserve a candidate, the exact capability gap must be escalated rather than treated as evidence that no suitable component exists.
spec.title: Bubble Break ASMR Tabletop
spec.summary:
Create a compact one-player Bubble Break ASMR experience centered on a reusable 4-by-4 sheet of 16 individually selectable bubbles. The player begins already positioned at a safe, collidable workstation with a close angled view of the bubble-wrap sheet; no travel or large map is needed. The first intact bubbles and a minimal “Popped 0 / 16” display are immediately readable. Clicking with a mouse or tapping on touch teaches the loop without a separate tutorial: the chosen bubble depresses, visibly pops, plays a synchronized Marketplace pop sound, settles into a clearly popped state, and only then increases the counter by exactly one.

Each bubble owns an authoritative intact, popping, or popped state. Intact-to-popping is accepted once; held input, spam during the transition, and interaction with a popped bubble do nothing further. Finishing all 16 bubbles produces clear sheet-complete feedback and exposes or emphasizes a deliberate Reset Sheet control. Reset returns every bubble to its fresh visual and interaction state and sets the counter to zero, allowing the short ASMR loop to repeat.

The space is a small bounded tabletop vignette rather than a map: a safe spawn/view position, one desk, the centered interaction sheet, a soft backdrop, and restrained environmental dressing. The server remains authoritative for bubble transitions, distance, rates, count, completion, and reset even though the intended session has one player. The client handles pointer/touch targeting, close camera presentation, UI, and local feedback through inspected component interfaces. State is session-only and rebuilt cleanly across reset, respawn, and player removal. There is no persistence, multiplayer gameplay, purchases, progression system, or unrelated activity.

Marketplace discovery and inspection precede implementation ownership. Existing verified geometry, behavior, animation, and media are preserved. Assumed reasonable details are a 16-bubble sheet, a compact fixed/limited tabletop viewpoint, warm neutral styling, and a two-step or equivalently guarded reset interaction to prevent accidental sheet loss. Questions are omitted because the user explicitly delegated incidental choices and the core loop is fully specified. Success remains pending native desktop and touch observation, including actual audio playback and listening; code inspection alone cannot pass the experience.
spec.visualDirection:
Use a close, calm tabletop composition with the bubble sheet as the unmistakable focal point. Place the 4-by-4 sheet centrally on a warm matte wood or light neutral desk, framed by a softly colored back panel and a few restrained, noninteractive desk-edge forms. Keep the playable area compact and bounded, with the player/viewpoint already aligned to the sheet so each bubble occupies a generous touch target. Avoid distant scenery, visual clutter, neon arcade styling, or unrelated props that compete with the tactile surface.

The sheet should read as a thin translucent or softly glossy base with rounded raised bubbles arranged on a precise grid. Intact bubbles need a consistent convex silhouette and gentle highlight; the active press should visibly flatten or sink before the pop; popped bubbles should settle into a lower, wrinkled, inverted, or otherwise unmistakably collapsed silhouette. Motion should be short and tactile rather than bouncy: a readable press phase, a crisp pop transition synchronized to sound, and a quick settle with no restoration until reset. A subtle selection highlight may be used for mouse hover, but touch must not depend on hover.

Use a restrained palette: warm neutral tabletop and background, cool translucent bubble material, dark charcoal text, and one soft accent color for completion/reset emphasis. Lighting should be broad and soft enough to reveal bubble curvature without hard glare. Keep the camera close and slightly angled from above so all 16 bubbles remain visible and individually targetable on desktop and common touch screens.

The HUD should be minimal and device-safe: a compact counter near the top edge, a small Reset Sheet control away from the bubble grid, and a centered but unobtrusive completion card or banner after the final pop. Use large readable numerals, short labels, high contrast, rounded panels, and touch targets large enough for fingers. The counter changes only after the corresponding visible/audio pop completes. Completion feedback should clearly acknowledge “Sheet Complete” and direct the player toward the deliberate reset without adding currencies, unlocks, or progression.

tasks.title: Discover, import, audit, and natively probe a complete Marketplace bubble-wrap interaction plus its captured media; record any source, dependency, animation, audio, or importer capability gaps before implementation ownership is assigned.

Compose the compact bounded tabletop, safe spawn/view position, sheet placement, soft lighting, backdrop, and interaction clearances around the retained component without destroying unrelated objects.

After inspection, preserve the retained component's verified interfaces and implement only proven gaps for authoritative per-bubble transitions, input validation, delayed exact counting, synchronized verified audio, completion, and fresh-sheet reset. Register exclusive script ownership only once the imported hierarchy establishes what glue is necessary.

Integrate the close desktop/touch camera and minimal persistent counter, guarded reset, and completion presentation against the authoritative inspected loop, with respawn rebinding and cleanup. Preserve any verified retained UI rather than duplicating it.

Run protected native gameplay verification on desktop and touch, including listening checks and observed timing/state tests; report every missing asset, capability, or failed interaction honestly and repair only through the owning integration task.
